## We Specialize In

Pet Emergency Care & Oncology in North Little Rock

At After Hour Animal Hospital, we provide emergency and specialized care for dogs and cats in Central Arkansas, including compassionate oncology services.

As a full-service veterinary emergency facility, we're equipped to handle your pet’s urgent needs with advanced diagnostics, a fully stocked in-house pharmacy, and around-the-clock staff. Our in-house lab delivers fast results, and we offer digital radiology, ultrasound, and endoscopy to support accurate, timely diagnoses. We also maintain critical emergency supplies such as snake antivenom and transfusion products.

For pets facing a cancer diagnosis, we’re proud to offer specialized oncology care with a focus on collaboration, clear communication, and tailored treatment plans. Whether we’re managing an urgent injury or providing ongoing support for a serious illness, our team is committed to delivering expert, compassionate care when your pet needs it most.

#### Jessica Mobley

DVM, DACVIM (Oncology)

Dr. Jessica Mobley grew up in the suburbs of Atlanta and is a proud SEC graduate, having attended the University of Georgia for her undergraduate studies, veterinary school, and specialty residency (Go Dawgs!). After veterinary school, she completed a small animal rotating internship at North Carolina State University in 2013, then returned to Athens for her medical oncology residency. She became a Diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine – Medical Oncology in 2016.
Dr. Mobley started a medical oncology service in Atlanta, where she practiced for the last eight years, and also helped establish other medical oncology services in Florida and Illinois. She currently serves as the Chair of Medical Initiatives for Thrive’s Medical Excellence and Education Department.
She is excited to be in the beautiful Natural State of Arkansas, providing cancer diagnostics and treatments for pets and their families!

Read Full Bio

#### Mark E. Sharp

DVM, CCRT - Medical Director

Dr. Sharp was born and raised on a farm in Muldrow, OK. He graduated from the Oklahoma State University College of Veterinary Medicine in 2001 and began practicing at South County Animal Hospital as an associate. In March 2002, he took over ownership of the hospital, which he has led since 2017. Dr. Sharp’s primary interests include referral orthopedics and neurosurgery. A lover of technology, he is continually seeking innovative ways to advance veterinary medicine. In 2015, he opened a referral-only practice in Fayetteville, Arkansas (Advanced Veterinary Surgery and Rehabilitation Center) focused on orthopedic surgery and neurosurgery. Outside of work, Dr. Sharp enjoys traveling and spending time with family and friends. His primary hobby is physical exercise.

## Going to Arkansas Veterinary Emergency & Specialists (AVES) in an emergency

Arkansas Veterinary Emergency & Specialists (AVES) posts 24-hour hours, so there should be a team on site whatever time you arrive. Call on the way in anyway — it lets them prepare for your arrival, and it confirms the overnight shift is staffed tonight. Posted hours occasionally change without the listing being updated.

Arkansas Veterinary Emergency & Specialists (AVES) sets its own prices. Typical United States emergency rates run $100–$250 for exam and triage, $800–$3,000 with an overnight stay — full cost breakdown, what to do if you cannot pay.

Suspected poisoning: call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on (888) 426-4435 (24/7, consultation fee applies) on the way in.
